Unit 11 · Advanced Topics

The PMM AI Tech Stack

Tool selection, build vs. buy decisions, and prompting mastery for the AI-era PMM.

The Tool Explosion Problem

When we evaluated AI tools for our PMM organization—fifty-three people across product marketing, competitive intelligence, pricing, and research—the exercise was supposed to take a week. It took three, because the landscape is overwhelming.

At last count, there were over 200 tools in the "AI for marketing" category on G2 alone—and that doesn't include general-purpose LLMs, developer-focused agent platforms, or enterprise AI suites. A PMM trying to build a coherent tech stack faces the same problem CMOs faced with martech a decade ago: too many tools, too many categories, too many vendor claims, and not enough clarity about what actually works.

The Three-Layer Stack

Layer 1: Foundation — General-Purpose LLM

Every PMM needs a general-purpose LLM assistant. Full stop. If you don't have a Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscription—or if your company hasn't provisioned one—fix that before reading further.

The general-purpose LLM is your Swiss Army knife: first-draft generator, research synthesizer, brainstorming partner, copy editor, data analyst, and format converter. It's not the best tool for any single task, but it's good enough at all of them that it covers 70% of what a PMM needs.

SAP Recommendation

Primary: Claude (best for long-form writing, nuanced analysis, maintaining context)
Secondary: ChatGPT (web browsing, image generation, broad capabilities)
Enterprise: SAP Joule (integrated with SAP ecosystem)

Layer 2: Workflow — Task-Specific Tools

Once you have the foundation, add task-specific tools that outperform general-purpose LLMs for particular workflows:

WorkflowRecommended ToolWhy It's Better Than LLM Alone
ResearchPerplexity EnterpriseWeb-grounded, citation-backed results
Competitive IntelKlue, CrayonAutomated monitoring, structured battlecards
Writing ConsistencyGrammarly ProBrand voice, tone management across teams
Content CreationJasper, WriterBrand guidelines enforcement, templates
Sales IntelligenceGong, ChorusCall analysis, pattern extraction

Layer 3: Integration — Connective Tissue

The most mature PMM organizations connect their tools into workflows that run without manual intervention:

  • Automation platforms: Zapier, Make, n8n
  • Knowledge bases: Notion AI, Confluence with AI
  • Custom agents: Claude Projects, GPT Assistants, custom RAG systems

The Build vs. Buy Decision

For every PMM capability, you face a choice: use a specialized tool, or build the workflow yourself with general-purpose AI?

FactorLean Toward BuyLean Toward Build
FrequencyDaily use by multiple peopleOccasional or single-user
ComplexityRequires domain-specific training dataGeneral knowledge sufficient
IntegrationNeeds to pull from multiple systemsStandalone is fine
MaintenanceRequires ongoing updatesRelatively static requirements
BudgetROI clearly justifies spendExperimenting or budget-constrained

Warning: Tool Proliferation

The biggest mistake we see: teams adopting a new AI tool for every task. Start with the foundation layer, get proficient, then add workflow tools only when you hit clear limitations. Each new tool has onboarding cost, maintenance burden, and integration friction.

The PMM Starter Stack

Essential (Start Here)

  1. Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus — Your daily workhorse for research, drafting, analysis
  2. Perplexity Pro — Web research with citations
  3. Grammarly Pro — Consistency and tone

Growth (Add When Ready)

  1. Competitive intelligence platform — Klue or Crayon for systematic monitoring
  2. Sales intelligence — Gong integration for call analysis
  3. Automation — Zapier or Make to connect workflows

Advanced (Mature Organizations)

  1. Custom knowledge base — RAG system with your proprietary content
  2. Agent workflows — Standing agents that run on schedule
  3. Integration layer — Connected systems that share context

Prompting as a Core Skill

Regardless of which tools you use, prompting effectiveness is the highest-leverage skill for PMMs in the agentic era. The same tool in two hands produces vastly different results based on prompt quality.

The PMM Prompt Framework

  • Context: Who you are, what product, what situation
  • Task: Specific deliverable you need
  • Format: Structure, length, style requirements
  • Constraints: What to avoid, what to include
  • Examples: Reference materials or sample outputs

Key Insight

The PMMs who get the most from AI tools aren't the ones with the most tools—they're the ones who've invested in prompt craft. Build a personal prompt library for your recurring tasks.

Key Principles

  1. Foundation first. Master general-purpose LLMs before adding specialized tools.
  2. Less is more. A coherent three-tool stack beats a fragmented ten-tool mess.
  3. Integration matters. Connected tools multiply value; isolated tools add friction.
  4. Prompting is leverage. Invest in prompt craft—it's tool-agnostic and compounds over time.
  5. Build incrementally. Add tools when you hit clear limitations, not when vendors pitch you.
